gaps.gap: High-impression pages stuck in positions 8–33 with near-zero CTR — missing compelling title tags, meta descriptions, and structured content depth to earn clicks
gaps.recommendation: Immediately rewrite title tags and meta descriptions for /correct-chair-dimensions/ (532 impressions, pos 23), /review/gesture/ (649 impressions, pos 10), /office-chairs-for-tall-people/ (335 impressions, pos 33), and /aeron-vs-gesture/ (190 impressions, pos 7.5). Inject tall-person specificity into every tag (e.g., 'for 6ft+ users', 'seat height range', 'tall people review'). Add FAQ schema and Review/Product schema to close the structured-data gap vs Wirecutter's 9-schema arsenal. These pages already have Google's attention — CTR is the only lever left to pull this week.

gaps.gap: No dominant 'best office chairs for tall people' pillar page — the top competitor URLs targeting this keyword are ALL dead (404s or DNS failures), leaving a vacuum your /office-chairs-for-tall-people/ page should own but ranks at position 33
gaps.recommendation: This is a rare short-term opportunity. Wirecutter doesn't target tall people specifically. Ergonomic Trends, Office Chair Picks, and RTINGS are all returning errors for this exact query. Expand /office-chairs-for-tall-people/ from its current thin state into a 3,000–5,000 word authoritative pillar: add a comparison table with seat height ranges and max user height, H2 sections by height bracket (6'0"–6'3", 6'4"+), internal links to your existing chair-specific sub-pages, and ItemList + Product schema. File a new sitemap submission in GSC after publishing to accelerate re-crawl.

gaps.gap: Chair-specific dimension sub-pages (/seat-depth/, /seat-height/, /tall-people/) are indexed and getting impressions but lack internal linking cohesion and comparative depth — no competitor is currently ranking a structured 'dimensions for tall people' content cluster
gaps.recommendation: Build a tight internal linking hub: connect /chairs/steelcase-gesture/seat-depth/, /chairs/steelcase-gesture/tall-people/, and /chairs/steelcase-leap-plus/seat-height/ bidirectionally to the pillar page and to each other via contextual anchor text (e.g., 'compare Gesture seat depth vs Leap V2 for 6ft+ users'). Add a standardized 'Dimensions at a Glance' schema-marked table to each sub-page covering seat height range, seat depth, back height, and max recommended user height. This turns isolated pages into a crawlable cluster that signals topical authority on ergonomic fit for tall users — a gap none of the live competitors are currently filling.

analysis.summary: Your site is already earning Google's attention across multiple relevant queries, but is hemorrhaging clicks due to weak on-page signals and thin content depth — not lack of indexation. The single highest-leverage move this week is capitalizing on the complete collapse of your top competitors on the 'office chairs for tall people' keyword set: Ergonomic Trends, Office Chair Picks, and RTINGS are all returning errors, leaving a clear path to own this traffic if you expand and optimize /office-chairs-for-tall-people/ immediately. Pairing that with CTR fixes on your high-impression, mid-position pages and a tightened internal linking cluster could realistically move 3–4 pages onto page one within the next two to four weeks.
